tally.title: The Hold
tally.director: THE PRECISIONIST (Fincher lineage). The camera never gets excited; the cut does. Insert shots instead of adjectives, procedure instead of promise, a clock under everything, tension held one beat past comfort and then released by the smallest possible sound. X0 Bot's two promises are a gift to this method: "you press pay" and "nothing goes live till you say yes" are not features, they are the pause before an action, and a pause is the most cinematic thing a vertical ad can hold. So these three films are built on withholding. A witness who answers in as few words as possible. A mess of speech corrected in silence. A world that holds its breath until a hand writes yes. Palette: black, white paper, one colour per film. No wink (the hero looks and waits, which is the whole brand in one gesture). No exclamation. tally.title: He had a team
tally.director: The Trickster. Handmade and surreal, after Spike Jonze and Michel Gondry: paper worlds inside real ones, the painted bot wandering into other people's footage, and in every spot one trick done in camera that explains the product better than a sentence. Three films: a torn paper window onto public-domain office films (manifesto); a whisper in a dark car whose fillers peel off the sentence like stickers (Keybot); and a fox in a library whose own paw presses Pay (the value: you stay in charge). Each has one job, each works with the sound off first, each ends on the fixed end card.

tally.title: Great at One Thing
tally.director: The Symmetrist. Every frame centred and level, mounted on white paper with a hairline dip-pen rule like a photograph in an album. Chapter tags with roman numerals. A narrator with a dry mouth. A fox who does not believe us. Nothing moves except the people and the type. The joke is always the point.

tally.title: Khaana khaya?
tally.director: The Humanist. In the lineage of Zoya Akhtar and Satyajit Ray: the everyday India of kitchens, trains, phones and the two-word message; Hinglish exactly as it is spoken, fillers and all; the small observed gesture over the big idea; dignity first, and the smile a viewer recognises from their own house. Three spots, three jobs, three different devices, one grammar shared with the campaign: what a person SAYS is handwriting (Caveat, white on film), what gets SETTLED is type (Geist), a bot's work arrives on paper, and a person always has the last word. Spot 1 is a refrain film built on the question every Indian family sends ("Pahunch gaye?"); Spot 2 gives Keybot a mother in Jaipur and a son in Bengaluru, one minute apart; Spot 3 finally gives the fox his voice as the family's sceptic uncle, and lets the brand agree with him.

tally.title: Leave at 4:40
tally.director: THE MINIMALIST. Three spots, one discipline. No screen is ever shown; no interface, no fingers on glass. Each film has one line of type, placed late, white on footage in the brand system (heavy Geist, two lines, no full stop, one word in Caveat, one brush underline in the bot's colour). Each film has one event: a hard cut into silence. Sound carries what words would have said: a low drone, a pulse that stops, the bots' bells ringing far off like a day being finished somewhere else. The only voice in the trio belongs to a fox in a library, and he is given the one question everybody asks. The set shares the campaign's devices sparingly and at a different scale: the taped card appears once, small inside a vast frame; handwriting appears once, under a spoken question. Everything ends on the end card as built, and in each case the card arrives as the loudest thing in the film: the paper sliding up into silence. Spot 1 is the manifesto (22.5 s), Spot 2 is Plan (20 s), Spot 3 is the value "you always press pay" (15.5 s). Footage that is not ours is described generically with search terms; nothing depends on a specific impossible shot. The power is in the frames being vast, the holds being honest, the type being one line, and the cut landing like a door.

tally.title: Count-In
tally.director: RHYTHM. I cut on the beat and let sound be the drummer; when the sound is off, the cut still is the drummer. Three spots, three tempos. COUNT-IN is a drum kit made of ordinary objects at 120 bpm, doubling until it breaks, then a rest, then the hero. ONE PLACE is five tempos at once that lock into one on a downbeat, for the Travel bot. THE SCEPTIC is a comic accelerando: a fox interviewee cut off by taped cards that answer faster each time, for the value "you stay in charge". Shared grammar across all three: the cut is a drum hit, the freeze is a rest, type lands like a snare, the hero is a physical presence over real footage, and every film ends on the fixed end card. Everything here is buildable from the three clips we own, generic open-licence shots, the synth kit, paper components and edge-tts.

judgments.coverage: ORDER AS A CAMPAIGN. Awareness first: 12 'He had a team' (global manifesto: a someone, now for anyone), 9 'Pahunch gaye?' (India awareness, the family refrain, with Plan and Travel cards), 5 'Great at One Thing' (the roster: all five bots named in type, the empty centre place filled by 'Yours / in one sentence', both owned clips reused). Consideration: 10 'Khaana khaya?' (Keybot, Hinglish, family), 16 'Talk Messy' (Keybot second flight, work audience, tone per app; ships only with 'Write clean' and a thinner pass), 1 'Leave at 4:40' (Plan), 7 'One Place' (Travel demo, Jaipur, the only kinetic film in the slate; ships with its Pay button and thumbprint removed and a train board), 17 'The Hold' (Travel assembled piece by piece, then the pause before pay: the bridge from product to trust). Trust: 11 'Uncle is right' (you always press pay, in India's own words, the hero nodding), 15 'The Witness' (they ask first, data not for sale, the team named again; global). WHAT IT COVERS: three awareness films that look nothing alike (torn-paper archive, stock refrain, mounted census); Keybot twice with Hinglish first; Plan once; Travel twice (one demo, one hold); the pay value three times at three temperatures (held, Indian, deposed) and the ask-first and data values once; India in 9, 10, 11, 7 and 16; every owned clip used (clip 1 in 5 and 10, clip 2 in 5, clip 3 in 11 and 15); the fox capped at two appearances, split by market so they rarely share a feed; the hero drawn alive in 5, 12, 11, 17. Lengths 20 to 30 s, all ending on the fixed card. WHAT IT MISSES: Code bot has no spot of its own in any of the 18 pitches; it exists only as a dotted head in 5 and a word in 15, and 'nothing goes live till you say yes' is never dramatised. Make your own bot has no spot; it is one line and a pencil outline in 5, so the activation end of the funnel is thin. Notes appears only as a card in 12 and 15; Spaces appears nowhere. 'We never sell your data' lives in one shipped film (15). Nothing under 20 s: there is no 6 to 10 s bumper family for short inventory, and 2 'Who Presses Pay' (15.5 s) is the obvious cut-down to build. Two Keybot spots over one Travel demo is a deliberate India-first weighting; if budget forces nine, drop 16 and take 13's hero flick into 10. Store and platform: no prices, no company names, no exclamation marks anywhere in the ten; the live risks are an airline name on a departures board (7), railway liveries (1, 7), a phone-maker logo (none in the ten), the gendered archive optics in 12, the flicker in 6 (not shipped) and the 'Send clean' claim in 16 (fixed before build).

COVERS. Awareness in four registers that do not repeat: what it is (12, archive through torn paper, the hero in every room), the problem it lifts (6, the day as a drum part piling into a scrawl), the roster and the one 'make your own bot' beat (5, the empty centre place filled by 'Yours / in one sentence') and the India-first emotional why (9, the two-word message). One spot each for Keybot (10, Hinglish mother to son), Plan (1, the only Plan pitch) and Travel (7, five strips into one sheet). Values three ways: 15 defines the team and states 'they ask first' and 'not for sale' under cross-examination; 17 shows the pause before pay with no voice at all; 11 lets the India sceptic win and the brand agree. The hero is drawn alive in five of ten (12, 6, 5, 17, 11), voice in five (12, 5, 9, 10, 15, 11 counts six) and none in four, Hindi/Hinglish carried by 9, 10, 11; lengths 20-30 s; every spot reads mute. Slate order is by funnel and differentiation, not raw total: 2, 4 and 13 score 40 and are left out because each is the same film as something shipped (2 is one exchange of 15; 4 shares its template with 5 and its ending with 17; 13 is 6's device on 10's beat). MISSES. Code bot: zero pitches across 18, a hole for a headline bot; 'nothing goes live till you say yes' is the same pause as The Hold and wants a sibling spot (a diff on paper, tests ticking, the bot waiting for yes). Notes: only a taped label in 12 and one word in 15. Spaces (family lists, trips, chats): nothing. Make your own bot: a six-second beat inside 5, no dedicated spot despite the brief asking for two or three on values and making your own. Ask any bot: a card in 12 and one answer in 15. No spot under 19 s (2 would be the 15.5 s cut and is best built as a cutdown of 15). Two fox films (15 cold, 11 warm): the fox becomes the campaign's sceptic-in-residence, which a campaign can carry, but a client who wants one fox should keep 15 and lose 11. Brand look is under-represented in 15 (black deposition grade) and 17 (cold grade); the end card has to carry the white paper in both. The manifesto group is Western in image (Prelinger office, stock census, stock drum); 9 is the counterweight and should lead the India flight.

COVERS. Awareness in three registers that do not repeat: 6 Count-In (the problem felt as rhythm, overload to relief, the hero arriving over real footage), 12 He had a team (the idea: having someone was always the luxury; archive as evidence; names Keybot, Plan, Travel, Notes, Ask any bot), 9 Pahunch gaye? (the India-first heart, love as logistics, Plan and Travel shown in passing). The team: 5 Great at One Thing introduces each bot by colour and verb, carries the tagline, and gives make-your-own its only screen time (the empty seat that fills with 'Yours / in one sentence'). Bots: Keybot twice because it is the flagship and Hinglish-first (10 the emotional two-kitchen demo; 16 the feature demo for tone per app, in a work register, not a family one), Plan once (1), Travel once (4). Values: 17 The Hold owns 'you press pay' with maximum force and silence; 3 The Sceptic covers ask-before-message, we never sell your data, and the deeper point that a thing which always asks needs no trust. Every spot works mute first; every spot ends on the fixed end card; the hero appears alive in 6, 12, 5 and 17, and the fox appears exactly once. Lengths run 20 to 30 s. Owned footage: Clip 1 in 6, 5 and 10; Clip 2 in 5; Clip 3 in 3. MISSES. Code bot has no pitch at all, which is a real gap: 'nothing goes live till you say yes' is the same pause 17 dramatises, and 17's grammar (held frames, cards, a hand writes yes, a stamp) should be re-cut for Code bot in moss. Notes exists only as a card in 12. Spaces (family and friends sharing lists, trips, chats) has nothing. Make your own bot has no dedicated spot; 5's beat is a seed, not a film. 'Ask any bot and the right one takes it' is a card in 12 and a line in 15, never shown. The computer platform (Notes, Code) is never seen. There is no true short: the briefest pitch is 15.5 s and nothing is under 15 s for high-frequency bumpers; 2 should be built as 3's cutdown to fill that. 'Plain words' as a value is implicit everywhere and stated nowhere. India-first versus global: 9, 10 and 16 are Hinglish, 1, 4, 6, 12, 17 are wordless or English, 3 and 5 are Indian English voice, a reasonable balance. Risks concentrated in the slate: three films (6, 12, 17) depend on finding many clean stock or archive shots, so build 17 and 12 first to test supply, and 5 and 3 as the safe builds.

check.verdict: Buildable and clearable after fixes. Every spot carries its 4.5 s end card inside its length, and no on-screen word breaks a store rule (no prices, no "best", no exclamation marks, no company or app names in type; the only names risk is archive insignia in the footage itself). The bible's one systemic build error is that its own type sizes do not fit its own lines: at the specified 0.085-0.09w cap height a headline line holds about 12 characters, and six headline lines run to 15-20; most taped-card lines likewise overflow the card widths given. Four VO tracks run over their seconds (01 one line, 03 the team portrait, 04 the mother's speech, 10 nearly every answer at Ryan -15%). One narrative bug: 05's train leaves while the walker is still on the platform, which mute reads as a missed train. One claim risk: 04 puts an English translation on Keybot's own card and plays a "sent" tick, implying Keybot translates and sends. Two headlines are unreadable where placed (07 white on white exhaust, 05 white on golden sky). 06 and 07 are the same film with the nouns swapped. Fix those eleven musts and the remainder is polish: two 0.028w grey lines nobody will read, lower-third type under platform UI, four openings that do nothing for 1-2.6 s mute, a Caveat bot card in 05, the made bot's seat moving between 03 and 08, and the two cut-downs needing assets the bible does not source.

problems.spot: All ten headlines (system: heavy Geist, cap height 0.085-0.09w, two lines, one Caveat word)
problems.problem: At cap 0.09w the font is about 137 px and Geist Black runs about 0.6 em per character, so one line holds 12-13 characters inside 1080 px with a 5% margin. Six lines are longer and overflow the frame: 'You always press pay' (09, 20 chars, about 1560 px), 'It finds the trip' (06, 17), 'Nothing goes live' (07, 17), 'till you say yes' (07, 16), 'Keybot ne likha' (04, 15), 'in one sentence' (08, 15). 'Uncle is right', 'A team of bots', 'They ask first', 'Pahunch gaye?', 'Each great at', 'when to leave' (13-14) fit only with no side margin. The three built spots' headlines are all 11 characters or fewer per line, which is why this never surfaced.
problems.fix: Add to the system: a headline line is at most 12 characters at 0.085-0.09w; a longer line drops to 0.07w as a named exception or is rewritten. Rewrites: 06 'It finds' / 'You press pay'; 07 'You say yes' / 'then it ships' (or keep the words at 0.07w: 'Nothing is live' / 'till you say yes'); 09 'Uncle is right' / 'You press pay' (drop 'always'; the small line keeps it); 08 'Your own bot' / 'in a sentence'; 10 use the bible's own fallback 'They ask' / 'You decide'; 04 keep 'Maa ne bola' / 'Keybot ne likha' at 0.075w for this film; 02, 03, 05 at 0.085w. Builders set Geist Black and measure every line before paper is drawn.

problems.spot: 01 He had a team, shots 1.2-13.8 (five 0.3w cards taped 'beside the first' in the paper margin; card 5 'Ask any bot' with five heads)
problems.problem: Five 0.3w cards in a row are 1.5w, half again the frame. 'Ask any bot' at 0.05w heavy Geist is about 500 px of type plus five heads inside a 324 px card.
problems.fix: Four cards at 0.2w (head above a 0.035w name) in a row across the lower margin, and the fifth as a 0.6w strip beneath them with the five heads in a row and 'Ask any bot' at 0.045w. The margin below the 4:3 window is about 770 px tall, so two rows fit with room for the hero's drop.

problems.spot: Taped cards: 02 shots 5.5-7.5 and 10-12 (0.5w), 06 and 07 hold cards (0.4w), 06 and 07 question card (0.8w, 'Pay for 2 tickets?' at 0.07w heavy), 09 shot 3.8-9 (0.5w with a Pay / Not now button row)
problems.problem: Ink Geist 0.045w is about 67 px type, about 37 px per character. 'Dinner at Nani's, 9 pm' (22 chars, about 800 px) and 'Pack a jacket, 11° there' do not fit a 540 px card. 'Flights found', 'Weather checked', 'Packing list made', 'Safe copy made' and 'One question, answered' (480-815 px) do not fit a 432 px card. 'Pay for 2 tickets?' at 0.07w heavy is about 1130 px in an 864 px card. 09's 'Pune, Fri 17:40' plus two drawn buttons and 'only you press this' overflow 540 px.
problems.fix: Size cards to their longest line plus 0.04w padding and say so in the system. 06/07 hold cards 0.6w; 02 and 09 cards 0.7w; 'Pay for 2 tickets?' on two lines ('Pay for' / '2 tickets?') or at 0.055w; 'One question, answered' on two lines. If a card must stay small, card text may drop to 0.035w, never below.

problems.spot: 04 Khaana khaya?, shot 1.6-10 (Caveat 0.075w 'wrapping line by line'; VO 25 words at Neerja -15%)
problems.problem: About 135 characters of Caveat at 0.075w is seven lines, roughly 1050 px, more than half the frame, over the hands. The VO is 25 words plus four '...' pauses; at -15% Neerja speaks about 2.1 words per second, so the line needs about 12 s in an 8.4 s shot. The flick beats at 10.4-11.2 then start before she has finished.
problems.fix: Write in a three-line window at 0.065w: when a fourth line begins, the top line slides up and fades (she is speaking; the screen is not a transcript). Shorten the line to 20 words: 'Beta... khaana khaya? Woh... Papa bol rahe the, Sunday aa rahe ho na. Bunty ka phone aaya tha. Theek hai, kha lena.' and extend the shot to 11.0; the flicks become 'Woh' at 11.4 and the stray 'haan' is dropped from the spoken line (or keep 'haan' and flick two words). Keep 24 s by trimming the son's shot to 13.0-15.4 and the paper to 15.4-19.5.

problems.spot: 04 Khaana khaya?, shot 12.2-15 (English line under the message on Keybot's card) and the 'soft sent-tick on the snap' at 12.0
problems.problem: An English translation on Keybot's own card says Keybot translated; translation is not in the product (filler out, punctuation in, names kept, a tone per app). A 'sent' tick on the snap, then a hard cut to the son reading the message with no thumb ever pressing send, says Keybot sent it; the copy rules say Keybot writes and the user sends. Both are 'nothing the app does not do'.
problems.fix: Move the English to a plain white 0.03w viewer subtitle at the bottom of the footage, outside the card, or drop it (the target market reads the Hinglish). Replace the sent-tick with a paper 'ready' tick, and change the small grey line on the paper to 'Speak in any app. Keybot writes. You send. Hindi, Hinglish and 50+ languages.' so the film states the division of labour.

problems.spot: 10 The Witness, answers Q1-Q7 (en-GB Ryan at -15%, handwriting on word times inside the clip segments)
problems.problem: At -15% Ryan speaks about 2.1 words per second and each full stop adds a pause, while the answer windows are 1.0-3.2 s: 'Writes. Plans. Finds trips. Ships code. Takes notes.' (8 words, 5 stops, about 5 s) in 3.2 s; 'Any. The right one takes it.' (6) in 2.0 s; 'They ask. I say yes. Then it happens.' (8) in 2.4 s; 'No one. It's not for sale.' (6) in 1.8 s; 'I don't. I don't have to.' (6 plus a 0.5 s beat) in 2.0 s. The handwriting cannot finish before each Q card slams.
problems.fix: Ryan at -5%, and answers shortened in the deposition's own spirit: Q2 'Writes. Plans. Trips. Code. Notes.' (heads pop on the nouns); Q3 'Any.' (one word; the head lifts on the clip's gesture); Q5 'They ask. I say yes.'; Q6 'No one. Not for sale.' (the claim still goes to counsel); Q7 keep both lines but run the segment at 0.6x (2.5 s) and take 0.5 s from the headline hold. Length stays 30 s. Re-time every handwritten word to the new word times.

problems.spot: 05 Leave at 4:40, shot 5-15.5 ('one person walking; in the last two seconds the doors close and the train pulls out')
problems.problem: A figure still walking on the platform while the train leaves reads, with the sound off, as a missed train; 'You knew when to leave' then reads as irony. The version that tells the story (the train arrives and the doors open) is written as a parenthetical fallback, left to whatever clip arrives.
problems.fix: Make the arrival the spec: the train pulls in and the doors open as the figure reaches them (queries: 'train arriving platform golden hour', 'metro arriving doors open', 'commuter boarding train calm'), or cut once at 9.0 to the figure stepping through open doors. If only a departing train can be sourced, the platform must be empty (she is aboard) with the shot-1 card echoed small in a corner.

problems.spot: 07 Go Live, shot 16.5-19.5 (white headline, lower third, over 'the exhaust filling the lower frame'); 05 Leave at 4:40, shot 5-15.5 (white headline over a golden-hour platform)
problems.problem: White 0.09w type on white rocket exhaust, or on a bright golden-hour sky, is unreadable on a phone, and the brand has no drop shadow or outline.
problems.fix: 07: keep the rocket in the upper half and put a thin ink letterbox or a 40% ink gradient behind the lower third (the Precisionist pair already uses bars), or set the headline in the upper third over dark sky. 05: deepen the vignette on the lower third or place the headline over the platform's shadow side. Add to the system: measure lower-third luminance before type; above 60% grey, add the ink gradient.

problems.spot: 01 He had a team, shot 11.2-13.8 (VO 'And someone to put him through to the right one.')
problems.problem: 10 words in 2.6 s is 3.8 words per second; at Prabhat -5% the line runs about 4.3 s, through the freeze at 13.8-15.5, whose silence is the point of the film.
problems.fix: 'And someone to put him through.' (6 words, about 2.5 s); the card already says 'Ask any bot'. Also start line 1 ('He had someone to write it down', 7 words in 2.6 s) at 1.0 under the tear so it clears line 2 at 3.8.

problems.spot: 03 Great at One Thing, shot 10.4-17 (team-portrait VO; bells at 11.4, 12.0, 12.6, 13.2) and shot 17-20.2 (closing VO)
problems.problem: 20 words with seven full stops at rate 0.9 need about 9 s, not 6.6; and 'Keybot writes. Plan remembers.' cannot be spoken in the 0.6 s between the Keybot and Plan bells, so the heads cannot pop on their words as written. 'Each great at one thing. None of them can cook.' (9 words) in 3.2 s at 0.9 is also over. 'He is great at dinner.' (5 words from 5.4) runs into 'Less so at the rest.' at 7.2.
problems.fix: Cut 'So.' and 'In a sentence.' (the label says it): 'A team. Keybot writes. Plan remembers. Travel finds. Code bot ships. And one you make yourself.' (16 words). Pops every 0.9 s at 11.2, 12.1, 13.0, 13.9; the outline draws 14.8-15.8; the hero looks to camera at 16.3. Voice only 'None of them can cook.' after the headline writes on (17.6), wink at 19.6; the headline itself is read, not spoken. Start 'He is great at dinner' at 5.2.

problems.spot: 06 The Hold and 07 Go Live (whole films)
problems.problem: One film with the nouns swapped: black, a 60 bpm clock, freezes with a card at +2.5 s, cut to paper, a Yes / Not now card, a 5 s wait with the hero, a handwritten yes, a stamp at 1.3 to 1.0 in 2 frames, a release at speed, a two-slam headline over the release, an end card without a wink. Both sit in Consideration and will run in the same feed. Secondary echo: 02 opens on a train leaving a platform at dusk with a Plan 'leave by' card, which is 05's whole film in two seconds.
problems.fix: Keep the wait, the written yes and the stamp as the shared trust device (that is the brand) and change everything around it in 07: open on the keyboard hands (the computer platform is the job), no black, the clock starts only when the hands lift; two holds, not four; the release is the control room standing before the rocket, so the two films cut differently; one slam, not two. Or make 07 the 15 s film: hands lift, paper, wait, yes, Live, liftoff, end card. Give 05 the train: start 02 on the scooter and put the archive train later or drop it.

problems.spot: 06 The Hold, shot 9.5-14.5 ('It waits.' grey Geist 0.028w) and 07 Go Live, shot 8.3-13.3 ('Nothing is live.' grey 0.028w)
problems.problem: 0.028w is below the system's own floor (0.03-0.035w): about 30 px cap, grey on white paper. These two lines carry the trust claim and will not be read on a phone.
problems.fix: 0.035w in ink, not grey, with a 0.3 s write-on; or cut the line and let the hero's eyes carry the wait.

problems.spot: All spots: headlines, small lines, subtitles and Q cards placed 'lower third'; 04 and 08 timestamps top-left
problems.problem: In 9:16 feeds (Reels, Shorts, Stories) the bottom ~14% and top ~10% of the frame sit under captions, handles and buttons, and the right ~12% under the button stack. A two-line 0.09w headline with a small line beneath it in the lower third puts the small line, and sometimes the second headline line, under platform UI; 04's and 02's gloss lines and 10's left-aligned Q cards are the most exposed.
problems.fix: Add a safe area to the system: all type between 0.12h and 0.80h and left of 0.88w; headline baseline no lower than 0.78h; small lines above the headline or beside the card, never below 0.80h; timestamps at 0.12h.

problems.spot: Opening two seconds, mute: 08 In One Sentence (0-2.6 static shoes), 06 The Hold (1 s black, then a still sprinter until 2.5), 05 Leave at 4:40 (still life until the tape at 1.0), 04 Khaana khaya? (still hands until 1.6)
problems.problem: Each opens on a locked frame with nothing moving and nothing written for 1-2.6 s; with the sound off in a feed that is a scroll, and the brief asks every spot to work mute from frame one.
problems.fix: 08: the hall lamp clicks on at 0.3, the timestamp types at 0.6, handwriting from 1.2. 06: cut the black to 0.3 s and tape the first card at 1.8 (the clock is not visible, so black buys nothing). 05: tape at 0.4, handwriting from 0.7. 04: first word at 0.8 and shorter '...' gaps.

problems.spot: 07 Go Live (NASA control room, Saturn V on the pad and at liftoff); 01 He had a team (Bell System switchboard films, railroad ticket windows)
problems.problem: The archive is public domain but carries marks: the NASA insignia on consoles and 'UNITED STATES' lettering on the Saturn V, Bell System marks in telephone-company films, railroad names on ticket windows. NASA's media guidelines also bar its insignia in advertising. The footage list applies 'no readable company name' only to the train clip.
problems.fix: Extend the 'cropped or masked' rule to archives A, C and E in 01 and to both NASA shots in 07: punch in 110-120%, mask or grade out lettering, choose frames without insignia; builders flag any clip they cannot clear before cutting.

problems.spot: 05 Leave at 4:40, shot 0-5 (Plan card text in ink Caveat 0.05w)
problems.problem: The system's grammar is handwriting for what a person says and Geist type for what a bot did; a bot's card written in Caveat breaks the only grammar the campaign has, on the film's single piece of information.
problems.fix: 'Dentist Fri 5 pm' in Caveat (what she told Plan) and 'leave by 4:40' in ink Geist typed letter by letter with ticks (what Plan did). The card then demonstrates the product in five words.

problems.spot: 08 In One Sentence, shot 12-14.5 ('the new head moves to the fifth place on the right') against 03 Great at One Thing, shot 10.4-17 (the centre seat left empty for 'Yours')
problems.problem: 03 leaves the centre seat for the bot you make; 08 says the new bot takes 'the empty seat the roster film left open' but seats it fifth on the right.
problems.fix: In 08 the row slides in with the centre gap and Coach glides into the centre; labels in 03's order (Keybot, Plan, Coach, Travel, Code bot).

problems.spot: 09 Uncle is right, shot 0-3.8 (VO 10 words at Prabhat -10%, 'paisa?' must land on the freeze) and vo_voice (en-IN on 'Theek hai', 'paisa', 'Sahi hai', no fallback)
problems.problem: 10 words at -10% run about 4.4 s against 3.8 s. en-IN Prabhat reads Roman Hinglish with English phonetics; 04 names a Devanagari fallback, 09 does not.
problems.fix: 'Bots? Let them find my train. But paisa?' (8 words), or move the freeze to 4.2 and shift the following beats 0.4 s (the warm freeze has the slack). Add the 04 fallback: hi-IN male (Madhur) fed Devanagari for the Hindi words, matched word count, or test Prabhat first.

problems.spot: 08 In One Sentence, shot 2.6-8.4 (Caveat 0.075w 'wrapping to three lines'; VO 15 words at Neerja -5%)
problems.problem: About 85 characters of Caveat at 0.075w is four to five lines, not three, and 15 words at -5% run about 6.3 s in a 5.8 s window.
problems.fix: 0.06w, four lines in the lower third; VO from 2.2 (the frame has nothing else to do).

problems.spot: 01 He had a team, end_card ('entered by the hero's drop: he lands on his bar as the sheet slides up')
problems.problem: The system fixes the end card; a hero who is falling when the sheet slides up and lands on the bar is a new animation inside the fixed card, and its first frame would show an empty bar.
problems.fix: He drops out at 19.0-19.4; the sheet slides up at 19.5 with him already on his bar (the drop became the arrival off-screen). If the landing is wanted, build it once as a shared variant.

problems.spot: 10 The Witness, shot 4.6-8.6 (heads 'clay, ochre, sea, moss, grey' on the five verbs)
problems.problem: The fifth verb is 'Takes notes', so the fifth head is Notes, which the system draws in ink; grey is the pencil of a bot you make. 01 draws Notes in ink.
problems.fix: Ink head with the low ink bell.

problems.spot: Cut-downs named in the campaign note: 'Face Down' (6 s) and 'Who Presses Pay' (15 s)
problems.problem: 'Face Down' needs a phone-face-down-at-morning shot that no spot or footage-list entry sources, so it is not a cut-down 'without new ideas'. 'Who Presses Pay' needs a fox segment and a Ryan line ('You do') that The Witness never records, and 'You do / always in clay' puts a headline in colour, which the type system forbids.
problems.fix: Add the shot to the footage list (query: 'phone face down on table morning light', 'smartphone face down wooden table'). Record the extra Ryan line in the Witness session. Set 'You do' / 'always' in white with a clay underline under 'always'.

problems.spot: Clip 1 (the cook) in 'Hands full', 03 and 04; clip 3 (the fox) segments in 10
problems.problem: The same man is three characters in three spots (a man dictating, 'great at dinner', the son in Bengaluru). The fox's 7.3 s covers about 14 s of screen in 10 with overlapping segments (2.0-4.4 over 0.0-3.1; 4.6-6.4 over 3.1-6.3; 5.8-7.3 over 6.3-7.3), so gestures repeat.
problems.fix: Accept the cook as the campaign's recurring man but do not run 03 and 04 in the same placement. In 10, alternate punch-ins (100/108/115) between consecutive uses of overlapping segments and never start a repeated gesture on the same frame.

problems.spot: 02 Pahunch gaye?, shots 3-5.5, 7.5-10, 12-15 (handwriting 'Reached?', 'Landed?', 'Pahunch gayi beta?' with no VO)
problems.problem: The grammar writes handwriting on the voice's word times, but these lines have no voice, so there are no times to build from.
problems.fix: Specify a cadence: 0.3 s per word, 0.5 s before the typed reply; typed replies at one letter per frame.
